transcript.text: indesit oven stoped heating, fan goes round n light on but its stone cold after 20 mins. grill werks fine tho. any ideas b4 i call some1 out

Yes — the most likely fault is the fan-oven heating element, or less commonly its wiring/connector, thermostat or function selector. A running fan proves the fan motor is doing its job; the working grill is a separate heating circuit, so it does not rule out the fan-oven element. Before arranging a repair, check these no-cost possibilities: 1. Make sure the function knob is on the fan-oven heating symbol — usually a fan inside a circle — rather than defrost/fan-only. Set 180°C and see whether the temperature indicator comes on.
2. Check the clock/programmer. If it is flashing or shows AUTO after a power interruption, set the clock and select manual mode, then retry. If it is most likely on fan-oven heat, the clock is in manual, and it remains stone cold after 15–20 minutes, an engineer should test the fan-oven element and its terminals first, then the selector/thermostat supply path. Don’t remove panels or work on the wiring yourself unless you are competent and the cooker is isolated from the mains.
ok tried those, its on the fan oven setting and clock is in manual, nothing flashing. orange light comes on n stays on but still no heat. what next?

The next likely cause is the fan-oven heating element. The orange light staying on means it is still calling for heat, but does not prove power is reaching the element. 1. Switch the cooker off at the isolator or unplug it, and let it cool completely. Look through/around the rear internal cover for the circular element. Do not remove any panels or touch wiring.
2. Look for a visible split, blistered section, small hole, or black/burnt mark on it. If present, that is strong confirmation the fan-oven element has failed. If it looks intact, it can still be electrically open. The remaining possibilities are a burnt connector at the element, the selector switch, or the thermostat/control supply. Those need an engineer to test safely with the cooker isolated. Ask them to test the fan-oven element and its terminals first, then trace the selector/thermostat supply path rather than replacing parts on guesswork.

isolated it at the cooker switch n took the back panel off (4 screws). theres a blister/split in the coil near the bottom with a black mark on it. so is that the element gone? heard a little pop from in there last time it worked too

[Heading: Likely cause: fan oven element]
I’m highly confident that is the fault. Leave the cooker isolated and do not run it again with the damaged element fitted. The usual repair is replacement of the fan-oven element, but the exact version must be matched to the full model number rather than the brand alone. The rating label is usually on the frame around the oven-door opening. If you can’t reach it now, that can wait. An engineer should also inspect the element terminals for heat damage when fitting the replacement; a burnt connector can cause a repeat failure. If you are not confident working on cooker wiring, use an appliance engineer rather than attempting the replacement.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
model is IFW 6330 IX, off the rating plate on the door frame. can i just fit a new element myself? ive done sockets b4, oven is isolated at the wall switch

[Heading: Likely cause: fan oven element]
Yes — provided you are genuinely comfortable working on an isolated fixed appliance, this is usually a straightforward replacement. The split/blister, black mark and pop are strong evidence that the fan-oven element has failed. Keep the cooker isolated at the wall switch and make sure nobody can switch it back on while you work. A replacement normally involves removing the element retaining screws inside the oven, easing the element forward, and transferring the two wire connectors one at a time to the new element. Take a clear photo of the wiring before disconnecting anything, and do not pull on the wires themselves. Before fitting the new element, inspect the two connectors and cable insulation. If either connector is blackened, loose, brittle or heat-damaged, stop and use an appliance engineer: the connector/wiring needs repairing as well as the element, otherwise a new element may fail again. Use a fan-oven element listed as matching the full model IFW 6330 IX, but check the seller’s compatibility listing and compare the mounting shape and terminal arrangement before ordering; do not rely on the brand alone. An engineer is the better option if the connectors are tight or damaged, a wire breaks, or you have any doubt about reassembly.
